brief: brief-js177-extraction.md: D-066's reopen condition 3. On a worker held to the i5-6500's speed by a CPU limit of 2, a synthetic 4K HDR job ran at 0.88x alone and 0.73 to 0.74x for the 24 to 28 s its worker's PGS copy ran (local disk), back to 0.88x 8 to 12 s after; three runs each. The job lost 8% to 9% of its CPU and 16% to 18% of its speed. Not in the brief: JS-154's dogfood sighting, 0.81 to 0.87 alone and 0.56 to 0.63 beside the extraction; that a job under 1.2x already asks for a helper (invariant 58). The brief's 'D-043' is DOMAINS invariant 43. Options: A void the sample and state the limit, B count it as load, C cap the extraction's CPU, D price it.
tradeoff: Nothing a viewer or operator has is lost; a protection is not added. Left as today, for the viewer of a heavy re-encode on a worker with little margin and no second worker with room: while that worker's own extraction runs (seconds on a local disk, minutes up to an hour for a whole-film read from a network store, once per file version) the film can run under real time and freeze, neither refused nor shared on its account. Unverified when decided: that a play held at 1.2x alone falls under 1.0x (computed); the fall on a real film under a limit, on the i5, over S3 or NFS, and under contention without a limit; why the speed fell twice as far as the CPU share; how often a household meets it; how long learning is blind during chapter pictures or an hour-long read.
entry: Condition 3 is met in the letter and decided: JS-177 builds A. A sample beside the worker's own extraction neither lowers nor raises a learned figure; it changes only what is learned, so a job slowed beside one still asks for a helper (invariant 58, existing checks unamended). A re-encode under 1.0x beside its worker's own extraction is counted and logged with a reason of its own; docs/running.md 'Sizing workers' and docs/status.md Known gaps state the limit with both figures. JS-177 criterion 1 gains one leaf: the longest a worker runs with every sample void and what an overstated worker's viewer gets then; over 10 minutes, a figure not yet learned is still lowered beside an extraction, or it returns as a brief. Criterion 4's last sentence is replaced. JS-141 keeps its place and moves to directly after JS-177 on the own-extraction reason counted on the dogfood more than twice in a week, an operator report, or JS-143's count showing more than a few image-track reads a week; JS-143 criterion 3 also records each read's length and the lowest re-encode speed beside it. BL-262 holds C, D and placement, with the unexplained half of the fall to measure first. The HEVC fallback row's over-price is not a reopen. Rejected: B (refuses plays the worker holds), C and D (mechanism unverified, a cost to every viewer for a harm not measured on a held play).
serves: PRODUCT.md: 'A heavy film uses the whole cluster's processors rather than stalling on one machine while others sit idle'; 'every failure is reported with its reason, never silent'; 'Where a capability can't yet serve every film, the gap is written down and planned, not left as a quirk.' DOMAINS.md invariants 43 and 58. Owner, 2026-11-22: nothing outruns the product. D-064, D-066.
